Summary: World Wide Worx forecasts SA online retail at R159bn in 2026, up 22.5% on 2025, reaching 10% of total retail for the first full year. 79.1% of adults have internet access but only 34.2% shop online, so there is still room to grow.
Children's toys are bought by 13.7% of online shoppers (World Wide Worx 2026 via V8 Media), but local baby and toy brands are small, handmade-led businesses with no public growth data.

Brand-level evidence only. Sealand Gear opened its 11th store and moved to a larger production facility in 2026, and SakSak reached cult status in about a year with a ~17% repeat-buyer rate (V8 Media).

Clicks raised its stake in premium beauty retailer ARC to 61% in 2026, calling it a faster-growing segment. Mordor projects SA cosmetics and personal care rising from ~$4.2bn (2026) to ~$5.97bn by 2032. In this list Love Kinks, Lelive, Skin Functional, Swiitch and Hermosa Flor show growth signals.

Small local categories. Gifts are bought by 16% of online shoppers, but no category growth data is available. Eyewear is mostly Cape Town sunglasses labels, and tech accessories are led by Volkano and Peachz.

Clothing has the most online buyers but grows slowly. Shein (21.5% of online shoppers) and Temu still compete hard, though Shein growth slowed to 11% in 2025 after SARS ended the small-parcel duty concession.

Category: Food & Beverage (incl. coffee, biltong, craft drinks)
Summary: Online grocery is booming (Checkers Sixty60 R25.5bn, +34.7%), but that money goes to retailers, not D2C food brands. Specialty coffee is crowded, with 75+ verified SA roasters, many selling subscriptions online. Little public data exists on D2C food brand growth.

Mixed to weak for local sneaker and shoe brands. Bathu faced landlord eviction cases over unpaid rent in 2026, and Veldskoen went into business rescue in Jul 2025 (since recovering, with US exports on hold). Drip relaunched with a Pretoria store and e-commerce in 2026.

Faithful to Nature, an online natural-products retailer, has grown revenue at ~33% CAGR over three years and reached 15 stores by Sep 2026. Collagen, women's health and period care brands are proliferating.

Home is one of the faster categories: Woolworths Home +14.0% and TFG homeware and furniture +8.7% (company results compiled by V8 Media). Litehouse scaled to 8-figure revenue on its own Shopify store, and online-only mattress brands (Sloom, Meelu, SleepSport, Fast Asleep) compete on 100-night trials.

TFG reported jewellery sales up 3.9%, in line with clothing. Most SA jewellery labels in this list are small studios with no public financials. Pichulik keeps launching collections and collaborations.
Yuppiechef (Mr Price Group) posted double-digit sales growth and market-share gains in FY2026, and growth continued in H1 to Sep 2026 across online and physical stores.

Black-owned natural haircare brands are moving from Instagram-led D2C into national pharmacy retail: Love Kinks launched in 87 Clicks stores across five countries in Oct 2025 and raised funding in Apr 2026.

The SA pet market grew 15.8% in 2025 vs 3.7% for overall retail (Eighty20). Woolworths bought Absolute Pets and Checkers grew Petshop Science to 185 stores. D2C brands in this list focus on raw, insect-protein and personalised food.

Fieldbar (premium cooler boxes) topped the News24 / Statista fastest-growing companies list in Apr 2026 with ~1,600% growth and R134m revenue in 2024. Local overlanding, camping and home-gym makers sell direct online.
